subject: Penetration retest scope clarification & re-eval request
messages:
From: Jill Tan <jill.tan@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Penetration retest — scope & evidence needed

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the update in product-security last week. Were preparing our internal risk sign-off and need a few clarifications before we accept the retest results from your vendor. Could you confirm the following: 

1) Exact scope and testing window for the retest (IPs, hostnames, services).
2) Whether the retest covered the fixes for the three high/critical findings flagged in the original report (IDs ACME-2026-001, -002, -003).
3) A signed verification letter or delta report from the third-party pentest firm stating which findings were re-tested and the results.
4) Any supporting artifacts (remediation summary, code/patch ids, PR links, build/release tags).

Wed like to complete sign-off this month if possible; if SecureLabs can provide the signed report + tested endpoints CSV we can mark the issues closed on our side.

Could you also confirm whether credentialed tests were used for the retest (and if so, what account scope), and whether social-engineering or phishing checks were included?

Appreciate a short checklist or attachments — a one-page delta summary is ideal.

Best,
Jill Tan
Lead InfoSec Engineer
Acme Analytics
[jill.tan@acme-analytics.com]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jill Tan <jill.tan@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Penetration retest — scope & evidence needed

Hi Jill — thanks for the clear checklist. Well get everything over to you. Quick summary of what we plan to provide: 

- Redwood remediation summary (one-page delta + list of PRs & builds). [Attachment: redwood_remediation_summary_20260610.pdf]
- Manifest of fixes and where they were deployed (service names + release tags).
- Third-party retest report from SecureLabs when they complete their validation: expected by end of day 2026-06-14.
- CSV of tested endpoints / IPs used during the re-test.

Notes: the retest will be credentialed for internal services only (service account with read-only DB access) — SecureLabs will not have privileged admin access. No phishing/social engineering tests were in scope for this round. 

Ive attached the remediation summary and a link to our remediation tracker for visibility: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B_remediation_tracker. 

If youd like SecureLabs to include a line-item in their report confirming the exact PR/build they tested (we can supply the commit hashes), please let me know and well request that from them.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Programs (interim)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_remediation_summary_20260610.pdf (PDF, 480KB)]
From: Alice Romero <alice@securelabs.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>, Jill Tan <jill.tan@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: pentest@securelabs.io
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Penetration retest — SecureLabs verification report

Hello Hannah and Jill,

SecureLabs completed the scheduled retest on 2026-06-14. Attached are the official retest artifacts:

- securelabs_retest_report_20260614.pdf (PDF, 2.8MB) — contains scope, methodology, findings re-evaluation, and a signed verification page.
- tested_endpoints_20260614.csv (CSV, 12KB) — list of IPs/hostnames and services tested during the window.

Summary highlights:
- Findings ACME-2026-001 and ACME-2026-003: fixes verified (no reproduction).
- Finding ACME-2026-002: mitigation validated; we observed the patch in staging but a low-risk residual configuration issue was noted (no exploitability in the tested environment). We include a short delta table in the appendix.
- Credentialed tests used a scoped service account (token limited to read-only access to the application DB). No social engineering was performed.

Forwarded for your records: 

[Attachment: securelabs_retest_report_20260614.pdf (PDF, 2.8MB)]
[Attachment: tested_endpoints_20260614.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

Please advise if you need the signed verification letter as a separate single-page PDF (we can provide that), or if the signature page in the report is sufficient for your internal audit.

Regards,
Alice Romero
Senior Consultant, SecureLabs
alice@securelabs.io
https://securelabs.io

Hi Jill — looping back with the artifacts from SecureLabs. Attached are the retest report and the CSV of tested endpoints; Ive also attached our remediation summary previously shared. 

Short checklist for sign-off:
- SecureLabs report: contains signed verification page confirming re-tests for ACME-2026-001/003 and mitigation validation for ACME-2026-002.
- Remediation summary: lists PRs and build tags deployed to production.
- Tested endpoints CSV: shows the exact hostnames/IPs and services included in the scope.
